output.page_summary: Project Nexus standardises links among instant payment systems. Polymer banknotes are presented as durable, secure alternatives that would coexist with paper notes. Cryptocurrency is described as a private blockchain-based asset without Indian legal-tender status. Money supply is introduced with an M0–M4 pyramid whose shorthand requires careful interpretation.

items.content: Project Nexus creates a single standardized connection between national instant payment systems, so countries do not need to build separate payment links with every other country.

teacher_understanding.question: What problem does the standardised connection address?
teacher_understanding.answer: It avoids the need for countries to build a separate payment link with each other country.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a shared standard simplify connecting payment systems?
teacher_understanding.answer: A system can connect through a common set of technical rules rather than designing a different interface for each foreign partner. This is interoperability between systems, not the creation of one common currency.

items.exam_note: Distinguish a standardised payment connection from a common currency or separate bilateral links.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग payment systems को जोड़ने का एक जैसा तय तरीका
terms.everyday_image: अलग phones के लिए एक ही तरह का charger port

why_chain.step: Separate links require separate connection arrangements with partners.
Project Nexus provides a standard connection instead of separate country-by-country links.

unpack.example_or_place: A national instant payment system connecting with systems abroad.
unpack.consequence: Interoperability can expand without rebuilding a unique link for each partner.
unpack.visual_verb: replace many pairwise links with standardised connections
unpack.level_extra: Ask whether the arrangement connects payment systems or replaces national currencies.

items.content: Plastic Currency Notes by the RBI
items.exam_note: Section heading.

items.content: These are the currency notes made from security-grade Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene (BOPP) instead of the traditional cotton-based paper substrate.

teacher_understanding.question: What defines these plastic currency notes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their underlying material is security-grade Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene, abbreviated BOPP, rather than cotton-based paper.

teacher_understanding.question: Which material contrast establishes the distinction?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page explicitly contrasts BOPP with the traditional cotton-based paper substrate.

teacher_understanding.question: How should a learner understand 'substrate' and 'biaxially oriented'?
teacher_understanding.answer: The substrate is the base sheet carrying the printing and security features. Biaxial orientation means the polymer film is stretched in two directions during manufacture to improve its properties.

prerequisites: material used as a printing base
items.exam_note: Know the full form of BOPP and the cotton-based-paper comparison.

terms.plain_meaning: दो दिशाओं में खींचकर तैयार की गई खास polymer film
terms.everyday_image: दो ओर से तानी गई पतली sheet

terms.plain_meaning: वह आधार sheet जिस पर note बनता और छपता है
terms.everyday_image: जिस कागज़ पर तस्वीर छपती है

why_chain.step: A banknote needs a suitable base to carry printing and withstand handling.
The page identifies security-grade BOPP as the alternative to cotton-based paper.

unpack.example_or_place: The material forming the body of a physical banknote.
unpack.consequence: Plastic currency refers to a change of banknote material, not a digital payment instrument.
unpack.visual_verb: swap cotton-based sheet for polymer film
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse polymer notes with plastic payment cards.

items.content: They are specially engineered polymer banknotes with embedded security features, not ordinary plastic.

teacher_understanding.question: How do polymer banknotes compare with ordinary plastic?
teacher_understanding.answer: The banknotes are specially engineered and incorporate security features; the page rejects treating them as ordinary plastic.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes being made of plastic insufficient for a currency note?
teacher_understanding.answer: A banknote must also be recognisable and verifiable as genuine currency, not merely be a sheet of polymer.

teacher_understanding.question: Why embed security features in a note?
teacher_understanding.answer: Features that are difficult to reproduce help users and machines distinguish genuine notes from counterfeits.

items.exam_note: Material and built-in security both matter; ordinary plastic is not equivalent to a banknote.

terms.plain_meaning: असली note पहचानने की खास चीज़ें जो उसके भीतर या बनावट में हों
terms.everyday_image: कपड़े में बुना हुआ पहचान का निशान

why_chain.step: Currency needs protection against copying.
These polymer notes contain specially engineered security features.

unpack.example_or_place: Checking the authenticity of a banknote before accepting it.
unpack.consequence: The material change also serves the anti-counterfeiting objective.
unpack.visual_verb: reveal security features within the note
unpack.level_extra: The page does not list particular security features; do not invent a list as book content.

items.content: RBI will start with small denomination notes such as ₹10 and ₹20. Up to 4x longer time span.

teacher_understanding.question: Which denominations and durability claim does the page give?
teacher_understanding.answer: It states a proposed start with ₹10 and ₹20 notes and a lifespan of up to four times longer.

teacher_understanding.question: Does this sentence prove that polymer notes have already been issued nationally?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. It uses the prospective wording 'will start' and provides no implementation date or evidence of actual nationwide issuance.

teacher_understanding.question: Why would low denominations be useful for assessing durability?
teacher_understanding.answer: Frequently used low-value notes pass through many hands, making resistance to everyday wear especially relevant.

items.exam_note: Retain ₹10, ₹20 and 'up to 4x'; do not convert a proposed rollout into a completed event.

terms.plain_meaning: कम face value वाले notes
terms.everyday_image: छुट्टे में दिया गया ₹10 का note

why_chain.step: Repeated handling wears down notes.
The page proposes low denominations and claims up to fourfold longevity.

unpack.example_or_place: Small-value cash changing hands at a shop.
unpack.consequence: Longer life could mean fewer replacements, not a higher face value.
unpack.visual_verb: compare note lifetimes on parallel timelines
unpack.level_extra: 'Up to' is an upper-bound claim, not a guaranteed lifespan for every note.

items.content: 2013: Government approved a field trial of ₹10 polymer notes.

teacher_understanding.question: When did the government approve the stated field trial?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page dates approval of a ₹10 polymer-note field trial to 2013.

teacher_understanding.question: Why conduct a field trial before wider adoption?
teacher_understanding.answer: Testing in actual use can reveal durability, handling and acceptance problems that laboratory checks may not capture.

teacher_understanding.question: How does approval differ from completed implementation?
teacher_understanding.answer: Approval authorises a trial; it does not by itself establish that the trial was completed or that nationwide circulation followed.

items.exam_note: Pair 2013 with approval of a ₹10 field trial, not nationwide replacement.

terms.plain_meaning: असल इस्तेमाल की जगह पर सीमित जाँच
terms.everyday_image: नई bus को पहले एक route पर चलाकर देखना

why_chain.step: A new note material must work under everyday conditions.
A field trial provides practical testing before a wider decision.

unpack.example_or_place: 2013 approval concerning ₹10 polymer notes.
unpack.consequence: Separate the policy milestone from claims about actual circulation.
unpack.visual_verb: mark approval on a timeline
unpack.level_extra: Approval, trial completion and nationwide launch are distinct milestones.

items.content: Existing paper notes will continue to circulate alongside polymer notes; this is not a currency replacement exercise.

teacher_understanding.question: What relationship does the page envisage between paper and polymer notes?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both would circulate alongside one another rather than polymer notes replacing the existing paper currency in this exercise.

teacher_understanding.question: How is introducing a new material different from withdrawing existing notes?
teacher_understanding.answer: A new material can be added while old notes remain usable. Withdrawal instead changes the acceptability or circulation status of existing notes.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must a learner keep these ideas separate?
teacher_understanding.answer: A change in what a note is made of does not itself imply cancellation of the older note's monetary status.

items.exam_note: Avoid equating polymer-note introduction with demonetisation.

terms.plain_meaning: दोनों तरह के notes का साथ-साथ लेन-देन में चलना
terms.everyday_image: wallet में पुराने और नए design के notes साथ रखना

why_chain.step: Changing a note material need not invalidate existing money.
The page explicitly retains paper notes alongside polymer notes.

unpack.example_or_place: A cash payment using either form of note.
unpack.consequence: Coexistence, not compulsory replacement, is the stated approach.
unpack.visual_verb: place paper and polymer notes side by side
unpack.level_extra: A statement asserting immediate paper-note withdrawal contradicts this page.

items.content: The main objective is to make Indian currency last longer, become harder to counterfeit, and reduce replacement costs.

teacher_understanding.question: What three problems is the change meant to address?
teacher_understanding.answer: The objectives are longer note life, greater difficulty of counterfeiting and lower replacement costs.

teacher_understanding.question: How can longer note life reduce replacement costs?
teacher_understanding.answer: When notes remain fit for use for longer, fewer worn-out notes need to be printed, transported and replaced over a given period.

teacher_understanding.question: Does harder to counterfeit mean impossible to counterfeit?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Greater resistance raises the difficulty of copying; it is not a guarantee that copying cannot occur.

items.exam_note: Three objectives; distinguish reduced replacement costs from a claim of lower initial manufacturing cost.

terms.plain_meaning: असली जैसा दिखने वाला नकली note बनाना
terms.everyday_image: असली label की नकल करके नकली सामान बेचना

why_chain.step: Worn-out notes require replacement and fake notes undermine trust.
Durability and security are intended to reduce replacement needs and copying.

unpack.example_or_place: The currency-management work of replacing unfit notes.
unpack.consequence: The rationale combines efficiency with trust in cash.
unpack.visual_verb: slow wear, block copying and shrink replacement piles
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer counterfeit-proof currency or reduced face value.

items.content: More than 50 countries use polymer banknotes. Australia was the 1st country to introduce them in 1988.

teacher_understanding.question: Which first introduction and date does the page identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies Australia as the first country to introduce polymer banknotes, in 1988.

teacher_understanding.question: What scale of international adoption is stated?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page states that more than 50 countries use polymer banknotes.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is international adoption relevant to this discussion?
teacher_understanding.answer: Experience in other countries can inform assessment of durability, security and practical use; it does not automatically prove that every country should adopt the same design.

items.exam_note: Remember Australia–1988; the country count is an undated page claim.

why_chain.step: A proposed material change raises questions about practical experience.
The page cites Australia's introduction and use by more than 50 countries as international context.

unpack.example_or_place: Australia, 1988.
unpack.consequence: Polymer banknotes are presented as an internationally used technology.
unpack.visual_verb: mark Australia and extend an adoption timeline
unpack.level_extra: First introduction does not mean every Australian note was converted in that same year.

items.content: Crypto Currency
items.exam_note: Section heading.

items.content: It is a digital / virtual currency created & stored using blockchain technology.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the page mean by cryptocurrency?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes a digital or virtual currency using blockchain technology rather than physical notes.

teacher_understanding.question: Which technology is explicitly named in the definition?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blockchain is the technology the page associates with its creation and storage.

teacher_understanding.question: How does a blockchain help explain digital ownership?
teacher_understanding.answer: It records transactions in linked blocks maintained under shared verification rules. The ledger records ownership or control; it is not a warehouse holding physical coins.

items.exam_note: Digital money is a broader category; not every digital payment is cryptocurrency.

terms.plain_meaning: लेन-देन के records को जुड़े हुए blocks में रखने का तरीका
terms.everyday_image: हिसाब के जुड़े पन्ने, जिनका पिछला हिसाब अगले से जुड़ा हो

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसी currency जो physical note की जगह digital रूप में हो
terms.everyday_image: हाथ में सिक्का नहीं, screen पर दर्ज balance

why_chain.step: A digital asset needs a dependable record of transactions and control.
Blockchain supplies linked records governed by verification rules.

unpack.example_or_place: A cryptocurrency transfer recorded on its blockchain.
unpack.consequence: The next distinction is who creates the asset and whether it is legal tender.
unpack.visual_verb: link transaction blocks
unpack.level_extra: Do not equate a bank transfer or UPI payment with cryptocurrency.

items.content: It is a privately created digital asset. It is not legal tender in India and is not issued by the RBI.

teacher_understanding.question: What institutional and legal status does the page assign to cryptocurrency?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is privately created, not issued by the RBI and not legal tender in India.

teacher_understanding.question: Which statements rule out treating this asset as RBI-issued currency?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page explicitly identifies private creation and says it is not issued by the RBI.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is 'not legal tender' different from 'illegal'?
teacher_understanding.answer: Legal tender is a legal status concerning settlement of monetary obligations. Lacking that status does not by itself settle whether holding or trading an asset is prohibited.

teacher_understanding.question: How is an RBI digital currency different on this criterion?
teacher_understanding.answer: A central bank digital currency is issued by the central bank, unlike a privately created cryptocurrency.

items.exam_note: High-value traps: private crypto versus CBDC, and not legal tender versus illegal.

terms.plain_meaning: जिसे कानून पैसे की देनदारी चुकाने के लिए मान्यता देता है
terms.everyday_image: उधार चुकाने में कानून से मान्यता पाया भुगतान

why_chain.step: Something may be owned or traded without having the status of official money.
The page separates private crypto from RBI issuance and Indian legal-tender status.

unpack.example_or_place: Comparing a privately created crypto asset with central-bank money.
unpack.consequence: Digital form alone does not confer official currency status.
unpack.visual_verb: separate issuer and legal-status columns
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer a blanket ban or a tax rule from this sentence.

items.content: It relies on a distributed ledger to record ownership without a central authority like a bank or government.

teacher_understanding.question: What performs the ownership-recording function?
teacher_understanding.answer: A distributed ledger records ownership without a central authority such as a bank or government.

teacher_understanding.question: Where are the records maintained in a distributed ledger?
teacher_understanding.answer: Copies are maintained across participating network computers rather than in a single central institution's record system.

teacher_understanding.question: How can participants agree without a central bookkeeper?
teacher_understanding.answer: The network follows agreed validation and consensus rules to decide which transactions and ledger updates are accepted.

teacher_understanding.question: Does decentralised recording mean there are no rules?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Removing a central bookkeeper makes shared verification rules important; decentralisation is not the absence of governance or checks.

items.exam_note: Understand distributed records versus a central bank or bank-maintained ledger.

terms.plain_meaning: हिसाब की ऐसी किताब जिसकी copies network में कई जगह रखी जाती हैं
terms.everyday_image: एक ही साझा खर्च का हिसाब कई दोस्तों के पास

why_chain.step: Without a central bookkeeper, participants still need an agreed ownership record.
Distributed records and validation rules provide a way to maintain that agreement.

unpack.example_or_place: Network computers maintaining matching transaction histories.
unpack.consequence: Trust shifts from one institution toward network rules and verification.
unpack.visual_verb: replicate and synchronise ledger copies
unpack.level_extra: A distributed ledger is the record arrangement; consensus is how updates are agreed.

items.content: Why Cryptocurrency?
items.exam_note: Introduces motivations rather than a practice question.

items.where_on_page: first indented bullet under Why Cryptocurrency
items.content: Some anarchist groups lost faith in FIAT MONEY because USA’s Subprime Crisis (2007) eroded the purchasing power of US Dollar.
items.type_note: The 2007 date supports a claimed motive for distrust; the sentence's main content is causal, not a timeline.

teacher_understanding.question: What motive for cryptocurrency interest does the page attribute to some anarchist groups?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page attributes their loss of faith in fiat money to the USA's 2007 subprime crisis and its claimed erosion of dollar purchasing power.

teacher_understanding.question: How can distrust of financial institutions make decentralised money attractive?
teacher_understanding.answer: People who distrust official issuers or intermediaries may prefer a system whose ownership records do not depend on those institutions.

teacher_understanding.question: What do fiat money, purchasing power and subprime crisis mean here?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fiat money derives monetary standing from state authority rather than redemption into a commodity. Purchasing power is how much goods and services money buys. The subprime crisis involved risky mortgage lending and defaults that damaged the financial system.

teacher_understanding.question: What caution is needed about the historical explanation?
teacher_understanding.answer: A financial crisis can undermine institutional trust, but its effect on a currency's purchasing power is not a single automatic relationship. The page supplies no evidence establishing its specific dollar-purchasing-power claim, and the motivation should not be generalised to every crypto user.

items.exam_note: Know fiat money and the trust argument; treat the page's crisis narrative as an attributed simplification.

terms.plain_meaning: सरकारी मान्यता से चलने वाला पैसा, जिसे सोने में बदलने का वादा ज़रूरी नहीं
terms.everyday_image: note की कीमत उसके कागज़ की कीमत से कहीं अधिक होना

terms.plain_meaning: पैसे से कितनी चीज़ें खरीदी जा सकती हैं
terms.everyday_image: ₹100 में पहले और अब मिलने वाला राशन

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसे समूह जो राज्य की central authority का विरोध करते हैं
terms.everyday_image: एक central controller के बजाय खुद नियम तय करने की चाह

terms.plain_meaning: कमज़ोर repayment क्षमता वाले borrowers के housing loans से जुड़ा financial संकट
terms.everyday_image: कई उधार एक साथ न लौटें तो उधार देने वाला भी मुश्किल में

why_chain.step: Some people distrust official money and financial intermediaries after financial disruption.
A system without a central institutional bookkeeper may appeal to them.

unpack.example_or_place: The page's reference to the USA's 2007 subprime crisis.
unpack.consequence: Connect the motivation to decentralised ownership recording, without treating it as the sole origin of crypto.
unpack.visual_verb: trace distrust toward an alternative ledger
unpack.level_extra: Separate financial-system trust, domestic purchasing power and exchange value; they are not identical.

items.where_on_page: second indented bullet under Why Cryptocurrency
items.content: They also dislike Banks & Card Companies because of transaction charges on e-banking, card payments, MDR, interoperability issues.

teacher_understanding.question: What other dissatisfaction does the page identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It cites transaction charges on e-banking and card payments, MDR and interoperability problems as reasons for disliking banks and card companies.

teacher_understanding.question: How do MDR and interoperability affect everyday payments?
teacher_understanding.answer: MDR, Merchant Discount Rate, is the merchant-side charge associated with accepting card payments. Interoperability concerns whether different payment systems can work with one another; poor compatibility can limit where or how payments are made.

teacher_understanding.question: Does this criticism prove that cryptocurrency payments have no costs or compatibility issues?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Cryptocurrency networks may also have transaction fees, technical constraints and compatibility problems. The paragraph describes a motivation, not a guarantee of a cost-free alternative.

items.exam_note: Know MDR and interoperability; do not infer that crypto transactions are free.

terms.plain_meaning: card payment लेने पर merchant से लिया जाने वाला charge
terms.everyday_image: ग्राहक के payment में से दुकान को मिलने वाली रकम पर कटौती

terms.plain_meaning: अलग payment systems का आपस में काम कर पाना
terms.everyday_image: एक system से दूसरे system के ग्राहक को payment पहुँचाना

why_chain.step: Charges and incompatible systems create payment friction.
The page presents this friction as another motive for seeking alternatives.

unpack.example_or_place: A merchant accepting a customer's card payment.
unpack.consequence: Links cryptocurrency motivations back to the page's opening concern with connected payment systems.
unpack.visual_verb: show a fee deduction and an incompatible connection
unpack.level_extra: MDR is not simply the interest charged on a credit-card loan.

items.content: Money Supply
items.exam_note: Section heading.

items.content: Money supply is the total amount of money available in an economy at a given point in time that people and businesses can use for spending, saving, or making payments.

teacher_understanding.question: What does money supply measure?
teacher_understanding.answer: It measures the money available in an economy at a particular time for people and businesses to spend, save or make payments.

teacher_understanding.question: Which wording identifies money supply as a stock rather than a flow?
teacher_understanding.answer: The phrase 'at a given point in time' identifies a snapshot rather than an amount passing through the economy over a period.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must money supply be distinguished from income or total transactions?
teacher_understanding.answer: The same money can be spent repeatedly over a period. Adding every payment would count its repeated use, whereas money supply measures the outstanding stock at a chosen date.

items.exam_note: Stock at a point in time, not income earned or payments made during a period.

terms.plain_meaning: किसी एक समय पर economy में उपलब्ध पैसे की कुल मात्रा
terms.everyday_image: एक समय की photo में पैसे का कुल stock, पूरे दिन का लेन-देन नहीं

why_chain.step: To assess monetary conditions, we need to know how much money is available.
A point-in-time measure avoids confusing available money with its repeated use.

unpack.example_or_place: Measuring an economy's money stock on a specified date.
unpack.consequence: Different definitions of what counts as money produce different monetary aggregates.
unpack.visual_verb: freeze time and count the money stock
unpack.level_extra: Money supply is neither total national wealth nor GDP.

items.content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) measures money supply using M0, M1, M2, and M3, with M3 (Broad Money), M4 being the most important indicator for monetary policy.

teacher_understanding.question: Which institution and aggregate names appear in this sentence?
teacher_understanding.answer: The sentence names the RBI, lists M0, M1, M2 and M3, identifies M3 as Broad Money, and then includes an ambiguously attached reference to M4 as the most important indicator.

teacher_understanding.question: What makes the sentence internally unclear?
teacher_understanding.answer: It first lists aggregates through M3 but then says 'with M3 (Broad Money), M4 being the most important indicator'. It does not clearly explain the relationship between these final two names.

teacher_understanding.question: Why measure more than one monetary aggregate?
teacher_understanding.answer: Different aggregates include different forms of money and deposits. Narrower measures focus on readily spendable balances, while broader ones include additional savings claims.

teacher_understanding.question: What standard distinction should an exam learner use to interpret the unclear line?
teacher_understanding.answer: M3 is the conventional broad-money measure commonly emphasised in Indian monetary analysis. M4 is a separate, broader aggregate including specified post-office deposits; it should not be silently substituted for M3. M0 is reserve money, a distinct monetary-base concept.

items.exam_note: Flag the printed ambiguity; retain M3 = Broad Money and distinguish M0 from public money-stock aggregates.

terms.plain_meaning: पैसे की ऐसी गिनती जिसमें तुरंत खर्च वाले पैसे के साथ कुछ और bank deposits भी शामिल हों
terms.everyday_image: cash और current balance के साथ bank में रखी fixed deposit को भी देखना

why_chain.step: Cash alone does not capture every monetary balance relevant to economic activity.
Several aggregates therefore count different sets of currency and deposits.

unpack.example_or_place: RBI analysis of currency and deposit balances.
unpack.consequence: The pyramid must be read through the components of each aggregate, not just its width.
unpack.visual_verb: sort balances into monetary aggregates
unpack.level_extra: The printed sentence is retained, not endorsed as a reliable M4-priority statement.

items.content: A white-outlined pyramid divided by four horizontal lines into five tiers. From apex to base: M0; M1 with 'Cash + Demand Deposits'; M2 with '+ PO Savings Deposits'; M3 with '+ Bank Time Deposits'; M4 with '+ All PO Deposits (except NSC)'. There are no arrows. Increasing width visually suggests broader coverage downward, but the drawing does not specify the base for each addition or define M0.
items.type_note: The image contains a labelled monetary-aggregate pyramid, so its content is a figure rather than non-teachable image boilerplate.

teacher_understanding.question: What does this pyramid visually organise?
teacher_understanding.answer: It arranges the labels M0, M1, M2, M3 and M4 from top to bottom, attaching currency and deposit descriptions to the last four tiers.

teacher_understanding.question: Which additions and exception are explicitly displayed?
teacher_understanding.answer: The displayed descriptions are cash plus demand deposits, PO savings deposits, bank time deposits, and all PO deposits except NSC.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the learner avoid a misleading cumulative reading?
teacher_understanding.answer: In the conventional Indian definitions, M2 adds post-office savings deposits to M1, but M3 adds bank time deposits to M1, not to M2. M4 adds eligible post-office deposits to M3. M0 is reserve money, not simply the smallest public-money subset of all the other tiers.

items.exam_note: Do not mechanically add every preceding tier; the pyramid is shorthand, not a full definition chart.

why_chain.step: Different kinds of monetary balances need clear grouping.
The pyramid offers a visual grouping but needs explicit bases for its plus signs.

unpack.example_or_place: Indian monetary-aggregate classification.
unpack.consequence: Read each labelled definition separately before comparing breadth.
unpack.visual_verb: highlight tiers and redraw the correct addition links
unpack.level_extra: M1→M2 and M1→M3 are separate branches in standard definitions; M3→M4 is another addition.

items.content: M0 — label in the topmost tier; no component description is printed.

teacher_understanding.question: What information does the apex provide?
teacher_understanding.answer: It gives only the aggregate name M0, without a definition or listed components.

teacher_understanding.question: Which standard monetary concept does M0 denote?
teacher_understanding.answer: M0 denotes reserve money or the monetary base: currency in circulation, bankers' deposits with the RBI and other deposits with the RBI.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should M0 not simply be equated with cash in people's wallets?
teacher_understanding.answer: Reserve money also includes balances held at the central bank, including bank reserves. Its institutional coverage differs from money held by the public.

items.exam_note: M0 = reserve money; its components are outside clarification, not printed in the diagram.

terms.plain_meaning: RBI की currency और उसके पास रखे खास balances वाला base money
terms.everyday_image: लोगों के cash के साथ banks का RBI में रखा balance भी देखना

why_chain.step: Banks need central-bank balances to settle obligations.
Reserve money captures currency and relevant RBI deposit liabilities.

unpack.example_or_place: Banks' reserve balances with RBI.
unpack.consequence: M0 is a monetary-base concept, not merely a cash-only tier.
unpack.visual_verb: separate currency from RBI deposit balances
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer a complete M0 definition from its position at the pyramid's apex.

items.content: M1 — Cash + Demand Deposits; the text labels the tier immediately below M0.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the M1 tier show?
teacher_understanding.answer: It shows cash plus demand deposits as the components associated with M1.

teacher_understanding.question: Which feature makes a deposit a demand deposit?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is repayable on demand rather than locked until an agreed maturity, making it readily available for payment or withdrawal.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the printed shorthand relate to the fuller Indian definition?
teacher_understanding.answer: The standard definition is currency with the public plus demand deposits with the banking system plus other deposits with the RBI. 'Cash' in this shorthand should not be expanded to include banks' vault cash as public money.

items.exam_note: M1 is narrow money; the diagram abbreviates the full component definition.

terms.plain_meaning: bank में ऐसा पैसा जिसे माँगने पर निकाला जा सके
terms.everyday_image: current account से payment करना

why_chain.step: People make payments using both cash and readily available account balances.
A narrow-money measure groups these immediately usable forms.

unpack.example_or_place: Currency with the public and a current-account balance.
unpack.consequence: Money supply is not restricted to printed notes and coins.
unpack.visual_verb: combine public cash and withdrawable deposits
unpack.level_extra: The '+' joins amounts, measured in the same currency unit; M1 itself is an aggregate label, not a unit.

items.content: M2 — + PO Savings Deposits; the label occupies the tier below M1.

teacher_understanding.question: What additional component is printed beside M2?
teacher_understanding.answer: The tier adds 'PO Savings Deposits'.

teacher_understanding.question: Which institution does PO identify and what is the standard base?
teacher_understanding.answer: PO means post office. In the conventional definition, M2 equals M1 plus savings deposits with post-office savings banks.

teacher_understanding.question: Why distinguish these deposits from the next tier's bank deposits?
teacher_understanding.answer: The deposit-taking institution and type of claim differ, so monetary classifications specify them separately rather than treating all savings balances as identical.

items.exam_note: M2 adds post-office savings deposits, not bank time deposits.

terms.plain_meaning: post office के savings accounts में जमा पैसा
terms.everyday_image: post office savings passbook में लिखा balance

why_chain.step: Some savings balances are held in post offices rather than banks.
M2 includes the specified post-office savings deposits alongside M1.

unpack.example_or_place: A post-office savings-bank account.
unpack.consequence: M2 differs from M1 by a specifically identified deposit category.
unpack.visual_verb: add a post-office savings balance to M1
unpack.level_extra: The printed '+' is additive shorthand; do not read PO as a commercial bank.

items.content: M3 — + Bank Time Deposits; the label occupies the tier below M2.

teacher_understanding.question: Which deposit category is associated with M3 in the figure?
teacher_understanding.answer: The M3 tier is labelled '+ Bank Time Deposits'.

teacher_understanding.question: Which base is used in the standard M3 definition?
teacher_understanding.answer: M3 is M1 plus time deposits with the banking system. It is not defined as M2 plus time deposits.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are time deposits distinguished from demand deposits?
teacher_understanding.answer: Time deposits are held for an agreed period and can have conditions or penalties for early withdrawal. They are less immediately available for payment than demand deposits.

items.exam_note: M3 = Broad Money; do not carry M2's post-office component into M3 automatically.

terms.plain_meaning: bank में तय अवधि के लिए रखे deposits
terms.everyday_image: एक साल की fixed deposit की receipt

why_chain.step: Households hold monetary savings beyond immediately spendable balances.
M3 includes bank time deposits in addition to M1.

unpack.example_or_place: A bank fixed deposit.
unpack.consequence: Broad money captures a wider set of bank monetary liabilities than narrow money.
unpack.visual_verb: branch from M1 and add bank time deposits
unpack.level_extra: The tier's position below M2 must not override the correct M1-based definition.

items.content: M4 — + All PO Deposits (except NSC); the label occupies the widest bottom tier.

teacher_understanding.question: What does the bottom tier add, and what does it exclude?
teacher_understanding.answer: It adds all PO deposits except NSC, explicitly naming an exception to the word 'All'.

teacher_understanding.question: Which full names and standard relationship clarify the shorthand?
teacher_understanding.answer: PO means post office and NSC means National Savings Certificate. In the conventional definition, M4 equals M3 plus total deposits with post-office savings organisations, excluding National Savings Certificates.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must the NSC exception be retained?
teacher_understanding.answer: An aggregate has defined boundaries. The fact that a savings instrument is sold through the post office does not mean it is included in every post-office monetary-deposit category.

items.exam_note: NSC is the explicit exclusion; M4 is not M3 plus every post-office savings instrument.

terms.plain_meaning: National Savings Certificate नाम का savings instrument
terms.everyday_image: post office से लिया savings certificate

why_chain.step: Broader measurement needs clear rules on which post-office balances count.
The printed M4 label includes PO deposits but expressly excludes NSC.

unpack.example_or_place: Post-office deposits contrasted with a National Savings Certificate.
unpack.consequence: The exception limits the coverage even of the widest tier.
unpack.visual_verb: add eligible deposits and move NSC outside the boundary
unpack.level_extra: In statement-combination questions, 'including NSC' reverses the printed definition.
